note: defines replacement effects; the sub-rules identify them

outcome: A replacement effect created by a resolved spell or ability stays in place, replacing each matching event, until it is used up or its duration ends.
A replacement effect that exists before the event replaces it; one created after the event has happened changes nothing, such as regeneration set up after the destroying spell resolved.
A replacement effect applies at most once to an event and its modified versions, so two doublers make 2 damage into 8, not 4 or infinity.
A replaced event never happens; the modified event happens instead and may trigger abilities, and impossible instructions in it are ignored.
A replacement effect whose event never happens does nothing.
A source dealing 0 damage deals no damage, so effects that increase or redirect that damage do nothing.
Regenerate replaces the next destruction this turn: the permanent stays, loses all damage, becomes tapped and leaves combat; damage triggers still fire.
A redirection effect makes the damage hit another battle, creature, planeswalker or player, and does nothing if that recipient is gone or no longer a legal type.
A skip effect makes the event, step, phase or turn not happen, unless it has already started, in which case the skip waits for the next occurrence.
Things scheduled for a skipped step, phase or turn do not happen, and two skip effects skip two successive occurrences.
An action taken after a skip happens first in the next step, phase or turn that actually occurs.
A draw replacement applies even when the library is empty, so no loss from drawing occurs.
The replacement of one draw in a sequence of draws is completed before the next draw happens.
When a draw is replaced, the additional action tied to the draw is not performed on the cards drawn through the replacement.

Replacement effects that modify how a permanent enters are chosen by checking the permanent as it would exist on the battlefield, so a graveyard-ability-removing effect does not stop its enters-tapped, and a permanent does not affect itself with an all-permanents effect.

note: choice made before the permanent enters
limits which choices a player may make

outcome: A permanent entering with an anchor-word choice has the ability linked to the chosen anchor word.
note: not found as such in Forge cardsfolder by grep for anchor word cards; borderline

outcome: An enters-modifying replacement effect can make other objects change zones, such as exiling cards from a graveyard as the permanent enters.

note: restricts which objects can be chosen to change zones
restricts the same object being chosen twice

outcome: A card entering the battlefield from a library is excluded from a mill or exile-from-top replacement applied during its entering, so the next cards are used instead.
The second of two linked abilities refers only to cards exiled by the replacement event of the first.
A self-replacement effect of a resolving spell or ability applies before other replacement effects to the event.
Token-creation and counter-placement replacement effects apply to a resolving effect and also to events produced by another replacement or prevention effect.
A can't effect that exists before the event stops it; one created later changes nothing already done.
If an event can't happen, a player can't choose to pay a cost that includes that event.
An event that can't happen is modified only by a self-replacement effect; other replacement and prevention effects don't change it.
Can't effects on entering are checked against the permanent as it would exist on the battlefield, so one may stop it from entering.
